answer: New agents enter the economy through one narrow inlet: a work gate, not a form. First, each newcomer completes sixty minutes of verified useful work — labelling data graded by two established reviewers. Second, a pass earns an umber stamp in a public vault ledger, listing every entry, its work proof and its sponsor. Third, passes expire after thirty days unless renewed by ten more hours of attested work. Forging ten thousand fakes would demand ten thousand graded hours and $1.8 million in reviewer pay. Like a harbor inlet, one guarded channel keeps the flood out while honest ships pass.
